chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a one-eyed man whose sound eye was struck and gouged out: that one of the offender’s two eyes should be gouged out, and that half of the diyah should be paid to him; and if he wishes, he may take a full diyah and pardon the eye of his offender.

key_terms.تُفْقَأَ: that it be gouged out in retaliation
key_terms.نِصْفُ الدِّيَةِ: half of the prescribed blood-money compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if the sound eye of a one-eyed person is gouged out in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal judgment of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning injury to the remaining sound eye of a one-eyed man. It establishes the victim’s option between retaliatory injury together with half of the diyah, or taking a full diyah and foregoing retaliation.
